raw_text:
Below is a gentle, progressive 12‑week postpartum return-to-fitness plan tailored to a 33-year-old client who is 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section, currently cleared only for light activity (walking), no abdominal work and no heavy lifting until the 6‑week check. The plan respects those limits in Weeks 1–2 (client’s weeks 5–6 postpartum) and progressively reintroduces core, full-body strength, and conditioning once medically cleared at the 6‑week visit. All sessions are designed for at-home training with a yoga mat and bodyweight only. If at any point she experiences pain, heaviness/pressure in the pelvis, urinary leakage, doming/coning of the abdomen, increased bleeding, dizziness, or incision discomfort, reduce intensity or stop and consult her provider. Encourage her to get pelvic floor PT clearance if available.

Structure and principles
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (A/B alternation) + optional easy walks most days. Early weeks are brief (10–20 minutes) and grow to 30–40 minutes by Weeks 9–12.
- Intensity: RPE 2–6 only in Weeks 1–2; gradually to RPE 7 by later weeks. Never push through pain.
- Core and pelvic floor: Begin with breathwork and pelvic floor connection; progress to deep core activation, anti-rotation/anti-extension drills; avoid sit-ups/crunches/planks until after 6-week clearance and only if no doming/pain.
- Walking: Start with short, frequent walks. Build duration first, then gentle pace.
- Recovery: Prioritize sleep, hydration, gentle scar/desensitization as advised by OB, and posture awareness with baby care.
- Equipment: Yoga mat; household supports (wall, chair). No added load unless cleared later; even then, use household items only if totally symptom-free.

Key safety cues
- Maintain neutral ribs over pelvis; exhale on exertion; avoid breath-holding.
- Watch for abdominal doming, pelvic pressure, or leakage; regress if present.
- Incision awareness: no movements that tug/ache at the scar; roll to side to get up.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2 here; postpartum weeks 5–6): Restore breath, pelvic floor awareness, gentle mobility, walking tolerance.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6; postpartum weeks 7–10): Foundational strength with deep core, bridges, hip hinges, sit-to-stands, wall-supported pushes/pulls; gentle low-impact cardio blocks.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–10; postpartum weeks 11–14): Build capacity: longer sets, controlled tempo, intro to modified planks/side planks if tolerated, step-ups, half-kneeling presses/pulls.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 11–12; postpartum weeks 15–16): Consolidate to full 30–40 min sessions, light circuits, more dynamic but still low-impact; prepare for future gym work.

Warm-up template for all sessions (5–8 minutes)
- 1–2 minutes diaphragmatic breathing, 360° rib expansion, 4–5 sec inhale, 6–8 sec long exhale through pursed lips; light pelvic floor “lift” on exhale, relax fully on inhale.
- Gentle mobility: cat-cow x 6–8, thread-the-needle x 6/side, ankle rocks x 10, shoulder circles x 10.
- Incision check-in: move within comfort, no stretch pain along scar.

Cool-down (3–5 minutes)
- Box breathing 3–5 rounds; supine windshield wipers; child’s pose with wide knees if comfortable; gentle chest/hip flexor doorway stretch.

WEEK-BY-WEEK PLAN

Week 1 (Postpartum week 5) — Light only per clearance
- Goal: Reconnect breath/pelvic floor, tolerance to short walks, reduce stiffness.
- Walking: 10–20 minutes most days at easy pace (RPE 2–3). Break into 2 x 10 if needed.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor connection: 2 x 6–8 breaths
  - Heel slides (supine, one leg at a time, maintain flat tummy, no doming): 2 x 6/side
  - Supine marches (90–90 not required; small range): 2 x 6/side
  - Side-lying clamshells (no band): 2 x 8/side
  - Seated scap squeezes (shoulder blade pinches): 2 x 10
  - Sit-to-stand to high chair (arms assist as needed): 2 x 6–8
  Session B
  - Breathing: 2 x 6–8 breaths
  - Pelvic tilts (supine): 2 x 8–10
  - Glute bridge (very small lift): 2 x 6–8
  - Standing heel raises holding chair: 2 x 8–10
  - Wall slides (back to wall, small range): 2 x 6–8
  - Gentle bird dog arm-only (on all fours, lift one arm): 2 x 6/side
- Notes: Keep RPE ≤3. Stop if incision tugs.

Week 2 (Postpartum week 6) — Still light until OB re-check
- Walking: 15–25 minutes most days, split if needed.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Breathing: 2 x 6–8
  - Heel slides: 2 x 8/side
  - Supine marches: 2 x 8/side
  - Clamshells: 2 x 10/side
  - Sit-to-stand: 3 x 6–8
  - Standing wall push (mini incline push-up): 2 x 6–8
  Session B
  - Breathing: 2 x 6–8
  - Pelvic tilts: 2 x 10
  - Glute bridge: 3 x 6–8
  - Heel raises: 3 x 8–10
  - Bird dog arm-only or leg-only: 2 x 6/side
  - Standing band-free row alternative: towel isometrics (hold towel ends, pull apart 10–15s): 3 reps
- Checkpoint: At week’s end, client sees OB. Only progress to next phase if cleared for gradual core and bodyweight strengthening. If not cleared, repeat Week 2.

Phase 2: Weeks 3–6 (Postpartum weeks 7–10) — Foundational strength (after 6-week clearance)
- Guidelines: RPE 3–5. No heavy lifting. Continue to avoid any exercise causing doming, leakage, or pelvic pressure. Build durations, improve posture and alignment.

Week 3
- Walking: 20–30 minutes easy-moderate, 4–6 days.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Breathing reset: 1 x 5
  - Dead bug arms-only (supine, legs bent): 2 x 6–8
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 8–10
  - Sit-to-stand (control down, exhale up): 3 x 8–10
  - Wall push-up: 3 x 8–10
  - Standing Y-T raises (no weight): 2 x 8 each
  Session B
  - Breathing reset: 1 x 5
  - Side-lying open book (thoracic): 2 x 6/side
  - Bird dog (opposite arm/leg, short reach): 2 x 6–8/side
  - Reverse lunge to slider-back tap or stationary split-squat isometric (hold chair): 2 x 6/side (small range)
  - Heel raises: 3 x 10–12
  - Tall-kneeling or half-kneeling anti-rotation press with towel (isometric hold pressing hands together): 3 x 10–15s/side

Week 4
- Walking: 25–35 minutes, include 3 x 2-minute brisk sections if tolerated.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug arms + heel taps (small range): 3 x 6–8
  - Glute bridge with 2–3s holds: 3 x 8–10
  - Chair squat (slightly lower if no symptoms): 3 x 8–10
  - Wall push-up: 3 x 10–12
  - Standing bandless row isometric (towel around pole, gentle lean-back isometric 10–15s): 3 reps
  Session B
  - Bird dog controlled: 3 x 6–8/side
  - Lateral step-to-stand (side steps, mini): 3 x 8–10/side
  - Split-squat supported (very shallow): 2–3 x 6/side
  - Heel raises single-leg supported: 2 x 8/side
  - Tall/half-kneeling anti-rotation press: 3 x 10–15s/side

Week 5
- Walking: 30–35 minutes, 1–2 days include rolling hills if available.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug alternating arms/legs (if no doming): 3 x 6–8
  - Bridge march (alternating foot lifts, tiny): 3 x 6/side
  - Squat to chair: 3 x 10–12
  - Incline push-up on countertop (if wall is easy): 3 x 6–8
  - Prone W squeezes (face down, forehead on towel): 2 x 8–10
  Session B
  - Bird dog with 2–3s pause: 3 x 6–8/side
  - Step-to-stand onto low step (bottom stair if available) or high knee march: 3 x 6–8/side
  - Supported hip hinge patterning (broomstick along spine, bow then stand): 3 x 8
  - Standing towel row isometric: 3 x 12–15s
  - Side-lying hip abductions: 2–3 x 8–10/side

Week 6
- Walking: 30–40 minutes, 1 brisk day (RPE 5).
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug full (if symptom-free) or continue heel taps: 3 x 8
  - Bridge with 5s hold: 3 x 8–10
  - Chair squat: 3 x 12
  - Countertop push-up: 3 x 8–10
  - Standing “pull-aparts” isometric (towel): 3 x 12–15s
  Session B
  - Bird dog: 3 x 8/side
  - Split-squat supported: 3 x 6–8/side
  - Hip hinge to wall (tap glutes to wall): 3 x 8–10
  - Calf raises single-leg: 3 x 8–10/side
  - Side plank modified on knees (start Week 6 only if no doming or pressure): 2 x 10–20s/side; skip if symptoms.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–10 (Postpartum weeks 11–14) — Build capacity and control
- Guidelines: RPE 4–6. Slightly longer sessions; introduce more anti-extension/anti-rotation and gentle tempo work. Still low-impact.

Week 7
- Walking: 35–45 minutes, include 5 x 1-minute brisk with 1-minute easy.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug 3 x 8–10
  - Bridge march 3 x 8/side
  - Squat to hover above chair (if safe): 3 x 8–10
  - Incline push-up (counter) 3 x 10–12
  - Quadruped shoulder taps (wide base) 2–3 x 6–8/side
  Session B
  - Modified side plank on knees 2–3 x 15–25s/side
  - Step-ups to low step or repeated high knee marches 3 x 8–10/side
  - Hip hinge to wall 3 x 10–12
  - Supported reverse lunge (range as tolerated) 2–3 x 6–8/side
  - Prone T/Y/W sequence 2 x 6 each

Week 8
- Walking: 40–50 minutes, one day at RPE 5–6.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug with longer exhale 3 x 10
  - Bridge single-leg ISO holds (one foot light) 3 x 10–12s/side
  - Squat 3 x 10–12
  - Incline push-up 3 x 12
  - Tall-kneeling anti-rotation press (towel) 3 x 15–20s/side
  Session B
  - Side plank knees 2–3 x 20–30s/side or straight-leg modified with top leg forward if ready
  - Step-ups or stair repeats low step 3 x 10/side
  - Hip hinge (Romanian deadlift pattern unloaded) 3 x 10–12
  - Split-squat supported 3 x 8–10/side
  - Standing shoulder “press” isometric against wall (forearms push up) 3 x 10–15s

Week 9
- Walking: 40–50 minutes, include terrain variation.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug or hollow hold regressions if strong (only if zero doming): 3 x 8–10
  - Bridge single-leg alternating 3 x 8/side
  - Squat with 2–3s down tempo 3 x 8–10
  - Incline push-up slower tempo 3 x 10
  - Quadruped shoulder taps 3 x 8–10/side
  Session B
  - Side plank progression (longer holds) 2–3 x 25–35s/side
  - Step-downs from low step (eccentric) 3 x 8/side
  - Hip hinge 3 x 12
  - Reverse lunge supported 3 x 8–10/side
  - Standing row isometric (towel) 3 x 15–20s

Week 10
- Walking: 45–55 minutes; optional 10-minute brisk block in the middle.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A
  - Dead bug 3 x 10–12
  - Bridge march 3 x 10/side
  - Squat 3 x 12
  - Incline push-up 3 x 12–14
  - Tall/half-kneeling press-out anti-rotation 3 x 20s/side
  Session B
  - Side plank 2–3 x 30–40s/side
  - Step-ups higher step if available 3 x 8–10/side
  - Hip hinge to air 3 x 12–14
  - Split-squat 3 x 10/side
  - Prone Y/T/W 2 x 8 each

Phase 4: Weeks 11–12 (Postpartum weeks 15–16) — Consolidate, prep for next stage
- Guidelines: RPE up to 6–7, still symptom-free. Introduce simple circuits and slightly more continuous work.

Week 11
- Walking: 45–60 minutes. Option: 10 x 1-minute brisk, 1-minute easy.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A (circuit x 2–3 rounds; 45–60s rest between exercises if needed)
  - Squat x 12
  - Incline push-up x 12–15
  - Bridge single-leg alternating x 10/side
  - Dead bug x 10
  - Step-ups x 10/side
  Session B (strength focus)
  - Side plank x 30–45s/side x 2–3
  - Hip hinge x 12–14 x 3
  - Split-squat x 10–12/side x 3
  - Quadruped shoulder taps x 10/side x 3
  - Tall-kneeling anti-rotation press x 20–25s/side x 3

Week 12
- Walking: 45–60 minutes, one day moderate sustained (RPE 6) for 15–20 minutes if fully symptom-free.
- Sessions (4x):
  Session A (circuit x 3 rounds)
  - Squat x 12–15
  - Incline push-up x 12–15
  - Bridge march x 12/side
  - Step-downs x 10/side
  - Dead bug x 12
  Session B (strength + control)
  - Side plank x 40–50s/side x 2–3
  - Hip hinge x 14–16 x 3
  - Split-squat x 12/side x 3
  - Prone Y/T/W x 10 each x 2–3
  - Tall/half-kneeling press-out x 25–30s/side x 3

Progression notes and modifications
- Progress by range of motion, time under tension, and control before reps. Keep breathing and alignment the priority.
- If any symptom appears, regress: reduce range, shorten holds, elevate push-up more, return to previous week’s version.
- If she acquires a resistance band later, you can swap towel isometrics for band rows and Pallof presses.

Return-to-jogging or higher impact
- Not included in first 12 weeks post C-section here. Consider a structured impact readiness screen and pelvic floor PT input after Week 12 if symptom-free.

Recovery, lifestyle, and postpartum care
- Daily “micro-mobility” breaks: 2–3 minutes of cat-cow, shoulder circles, hip flexor stretch, especially after feeds.
- Scar and core: Gentle scar desensitization only when fully healed and cleared; avoid aggressive stretching. Continue diaphragmatic breathing daily.
- Sleep and load management: Prioritize naps/sleep; spread housework loads; lift baby close to body, exhale as you stand; avoid holding breath with car seat.
- Hydration: Aim ~2–3 liters/day, plus more if breastfeeding; include electrolytes if desired.
- Nutrition basics (general, not medical advice):
  - Emphasize protein at each meal (aim 20–30 g), fiber-rich carbs, colorful produce, healthy fats.
  - If breastfeeding, add ~300–500 kcal/day as needed; listen to hunger/thirst cues.
  - Consider vitamin D and prenatal/POSTnatal per provider’s guidance.
- Red flags to refer: Sharp abdominal or pelvic pain, increasing lochia/bleeding after exercise, fever, wound changes, persistent urinary/fecal incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse symptoms (heaviness/bulge), or diastasis recti doming that doesn’t improve with cueing.

This plan keeps Weeks 1–2 strictly within “light activity, no abs, no heavy lifting” until the 6‑week check, then advances gradually. Adjust volume to her day-to-day energy and recovery, and when in doubt, choose the easier option and build slowly.
